# Jurgen Halili — Portfolio

> Freelance full-stack software engineer based in Kiel, Germany. Builds AI-driven products end-to-end — agent runtimes, multi-LLM pipelines, React Native, Postgres. Microsoft Dynamics 365 / Business Central on the other rail. Available for freelance contracts in Germany and remote-EU, 2026. Last updated 2026-05-14.

## Projects (10 production projects)

- [KeepItUp](https://jurgenhalili.dev/projects/keepitup) — Self-hosted AI agent that auto-fixes broken deployments. Stack: React 19, Anthropic + OpenAI + Gemini, Tree-sitter. Status: shipped.
- [Ëndërrat e Mia](https://jurgenhalili.dev/projects/enderrat-e-mia) — AI bedtime stories in Albanian, illustrated and read aloud. Stack: Expo + RN, Claude Haiku + Flux, RevenueCat. Status: in-progress.
- [GymApp](https://jurgenhalili.dev/projects/gym-app) — White-label gym OS — NFC entry, member app, multi-tenant admin. Stack: Express + Postgres, Socket.io + Redis, Expo + MUI. Status: shipped.
- [Pilates Studio](https://jurgenhalili.dev/projects/pilates-studio) — Boutique studio platform — admin web, mobile app, API, 594 tests. Stack: pnpm monorepo, Express + Prisma, Turso + libSQL. Status: shipped.
- [CleanSlate](https://jurgenhalili.dev/projects/cleanslate) — $20/month operating system for cleaning businesses. Stack: Next.js 16, Supabase + RLS, Telnyx + LemonSqueezy. Status: shipped.
- [Social Command Center](https://jurgenhalili.dev/projects/social-command-center) — Industrial Instagram content for any brand — autonomous, multi-tenant. Stack: Next.js 16, BullMQ + Drizzle, OpenAI + Postiz. Status: in-progress.
- [Reel Farmer](https://jurgenhalili.dev/projects/reel-farmer) — Self-hosted YouTube → TikTok pipeline. One command, multi-account. Stack: Bun + TS, Whisper + Gemini, Remotion + Puppeteer. Status: shipped.
- [Dabei](https://jurgenhalili.dev/projects/dabei) — Kiel's social pulse — find or start hangouts on a live map. Stack: Expo + RN 0.83, Supabase + Realtime, react-native-maps. Status: in-progress.
- [Websites](https://jurgenhalili.dev/projects/websites) — Three brand sites — Three.js hero, MongoDB CRM, fitness coaching. Stack: React + Vite, Three.js + Framer, MongoDB Atlas. Status: shipped.
- [advance.al](https://jurgenhalili.dev/projects/advance-al) — Albania's job marketplace — AI CV generation, AI profile-fill, embedding-ranked matching, auto-notify on match. Stack: React 18 + Vite, Express + MongoDB, OpenAI embeddings. Status: shipped.

## Notes (technical writeups)

- [Two-layer reasoning for autonomous AI agents — how KeepItUp gates a fix before it PRs](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/keepitup-two-layer-reasoning): how the autonomous SRE agent runs two LLM passes against the same broken build — tree-sitter AST slicing for context, a separate Reviewer agent that scores the diff cold, ≥85% confidence to PR (or ≥70% with build verification), three providers (Anthropic / OpenAI / Gemini) behind one budget-gated client.
- [Resumable pipelines: how Reel Farmer survives a crash mid-render](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/reel-farmer-resumable-pipelines): deterministic `data/runs/<run-id>/` file tree plus SQLite checkpoint database makes a six-stage Bun pipeline resumable from any failed step — paths as contracts, no queues, no event buses.
- [Vector embeddings for job-matching — why pure cosine similarity isn't enough](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/advance-al-vector-embeddings-job-matching): how advance.al pairs OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` cosine ranking with a 7-dimension explainable score (title, skills, experience, location, education, salary, availability) so the employer dashboard can show why a candidate scored 78.
- [Same schema, different databases — the Prisma adapter swap in Pilates Studio](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/prisma-adapter-swap-dev-prod-parity): better-sqlite3 in dev, Turso (libsql) in prod, one Prisma schema, two-line adapter config. 21 models, 594 tests, same Express app shipping as Vercel catch-all in prod and long-lived server locally.
- [RLS as a subscription gate — letting Postgres turn off trial accounts for you](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/rls-subscription-gate-cleanslate): CleanSlate moves the subscription expiry check into Supabase RLS policies. When the trial ends, INSERTs fail at the database; the UI doesn't run a check, the read-only state is automatic.
- [Hiring a freelance full-stack engineer in Germany — a 2026 evaluation checklist](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/hiring-freelance-full-stack-engineer-germany-2026-checklist): what to actually look for when hiring a freelance full-stack engineer in Germany — public repo evaluation, test discipline, deploy ownership, last-incident storytelling, and the two German-market specifics (Scheinselbständigkeit, Stundensatz vs Werkvertrag) clients usually aren't warned about.
- [Hiring a freelance Next.js developer — 7 questions that filter the field](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/hiring-freelance-nextjs-developer-7-questions): App Router vs Pages Router, Server vs Client Components, edge data fetching, CSP for blob workers, sitemap shipping, ISR vs SSG vs SSR vs Edge, worst-gotcha story. Five-minute screen that separates people who've shipped Next.js from people who've watched the tutorial.
- [Hiring a freelance AI engineer in 2026 — portfolio red flags and green flags](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/hiring-freelance-ai-engineer-2026-portfolio-flags): what to look for when evaluating a freelance AI engineer's portfolio — production agents not demos, named failure modes, multi-provider routing, cost telemetry, eval frameworks. Red flags include single Streamlit apps, vague answers on cost monitoring, and any mention of \"AGI\".
- [Tree-sitter AST slicing as a context-budget lever for AI agents](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/tree-sitter-ast-slicing-context-budget): why a 3,000-token AST slice routinely beats a 30,000-token whole-module dump for AI code-fix agents. Tree-sitter parsers across six languages with one query API, 50-500 line slices anchored on AST nodes, structurally-coherent context that respects function and class boundaries.
- [Three-model atomic content pipelines — text, image, and audio without orphans](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/three-model-atomic-content-pipelines): how Ëndërrat e Mia composes Claude Haiku (Albanian text) + fal.ai Flux Schnell (watercolor illustrations) + ElevenLabs (narration) into one transaction. Pipeline-level retries, end-to-end validation, automatic credit refunds on any stage failure.
- [Hiring a freelance React Native developer in Germany — a scope template](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/hiring-freelance-react-native-developer-germany): five questions that change the estimate by an order of magnitude — platforms, Expo workflow choice, native modules required, deploy/signing story, offline-first requirements. Plus a red-flag / green-flag table.
- [Hiring a freelance Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central contractor in Germany — what to evaluate](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/freelance-business-central-d365-germany-contractor): three tiers of BC contractors (config-only, AL extension, full-stack including integrations), how to tell which tier you're talking to, German-market specifics (DATEV, GoBD, ELSTER), and where to find tier-3 contractors.
- [Freelance vs agency for a software MVP — a 2026 comparison](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/freelance-vs-agency-software-mvp-2026): the decision framework — when solo freelance engineers win, when agencies win, the actual cost comparison, hybrid models worth considering.
- [Solo developer vs team of three — when each ships faster](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/solo-developer-vs-team-of-three-when-each-ships-faster): Brooks's Law at small scale, coordination overhead by team size, when solo wins, when three people win, hidden cost of team-of-three for MVPs.
- [Where to find freelance software developers in Germany — 2026 guide](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/where-to-find-freelance-software-developers-germany-2026): six channels ranked by signal quality — personal portfolios, GitHub outreach, Toptal/Malt, freelance.de/Freelancermap, LinkedIn, Upwork. With effort and platform-margin trade-offs.
- [The freelance developer due-diligence checklist — code, tests, deploys, security](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/freelance-developer-due-diligence-checklist): the 20-minute technical pass that catches the bottom 80% of bad freelance hires. Four categories with specific things to look at in each.
- [Freelance vs Festanstellung — a 2026 reality check for software engineers in Germany](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/freelance-vs-festanstellung-2026-germany): the hidden math — Krankenversicherung, vacation, sick pay, pension contributions, Scheinselbständigkeit risk — that turns a 2-3x gross-rate gap into a 1.5-1.8x real one.
- [Build verification beats raw confidence — why test suites outweigh self-reports](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/build-verification-beats-raw-confidence-scores): KeepItUp's confidence-gate relaxation rule — ≥85% default drops to ≥70% if the proposed diff passes the test suite in a sandboxed container. A passing test suite is a stronger correctness signal than any model's self-report.
- [Multi-provider routing — running Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gemini behind one client](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/multi-provider-routing-anthropic-openai-gemini): the LLM equivalent of an HTTP client with retries and circuit breakers. Stage-based routing, budget gates, per-call cost telemetry, fallback on outage.
- [Cost telemetry per LLM call — what to actually measure](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/cost-telemetry-per-llm-call-what-to-measure): minimum per-call fields, useful aggregations, anomaly detection thresholds. The setup that lets you defend a $30,000 OpenAI bill.
- [Why an AI agent should run Semgrep, Trivy, and Gitleaks before opening a PR](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/semgrep-trivy-gitleaks-pre-pr-docker): pre-PR security-scan pipeline running in Docker. Catches the specific failure mode of an LLM regenerating code that originally had an API key inlined.
- [Polling six deploy platforms 24/7 — API patterns that don't get rate-limited](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/polling-six-deploy-platforms-without-rate-limit-hell): webhooks first, adaptive polling intervals, exponential backoff, shared token bucket across workers, tuned TTLs per platform.
- [Stealth puppeteer and multi-account uploaders — the TikTok compliance-flag dance](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/stealth-puppeteer-multi-account-tiktok-compliance): puppeteer-extra-plugin-stealth for fingerprint normalization, persistent cookie jars per account, realistic typing/clicking cadence, residential proxies when needed. account-manager.ts hides it all behind one upload() API.
- [Remotion video rendering with the same components as the app — brand consistency without two codebases](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/remotion-programmatic-video-rendering-app-components): use the same React components in your Remotion compositions as your production app. Brand consistency is structural, not procedural. Reel Farmer + Ëndërrat ad pipelines.
- [Whisper model size — when bigger isn't worth the GPU](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/whisper-model-size-when-bigger-isnt-worth-it): six sizes (tiny to large-v3). Pipeline-context use cases tolerate small/base; user-facing transcripts need medium/large; multilingual content needs medium minimum. Cost vs quality breakdown.
- [Gemini clip selection — getting an LLM to pick highlights with the transcript in context](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/gemini-clip-selection-transcript-context): Gemini's long context (1M+ tokens) makes it the right model for podcast-clip selection. Output schema, heuristics that filter bad picks, human-in-loop review pattern.
- [The transaction ledger — unifying ads, subscriptions, and purchases into one accounting story](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/transaction-ledger-unified-credits-mobile-app): four sources of credits (RevenueCat, AdMob, IAP, free trial) → one Transaction table. Balance is SUM(amount). Refunds are positive rows. Fraud + churn queries become single queries.
- [Embedding worker on a heartbeat process — the pattern that keeps a matching engine honest](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/embedding-worker-heartbeat-process-pattern): PM2-isolated embedding worker + 60-second heartbeat + 10-minute alert threshold. Catches the silent-stop failure mode that infrastructure monitoring alone misses.
- [OpenAI structured extraction — auto-filling profiles from any CV format](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/openai-structured-extraction-profile-autofill): pdfjs-dist + mammoth + OpenAI JSON-mode + confidence routing. The flow that turns a CV upload into a match-ready profile in under 10 seconds.
- [Bilingual embeddings and the category boost — when one vector space isn't enough](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/bilingual-embedding-category-boost): OpenAI embeddings work across languages but vocabulary depth differs. A coarse-category additive boost cancels the bias for low-resource-language profiles against high-resource-language jobs. ~18% application rate lift.
- [Drift detection in a vector matching engine — when the model has changed](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/drift-detection-vector-matching-engine): OpenAI deprecates embedding models. advance.al watches per-candidate top-N stability + alerts on > 2× baseline turnover. The 7-dimension explainable score keeps the UX stable during migrations.
- [White-label as a runtime config, not a build step — how one app becomes many](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/white-label-runtime-config-vs-build-step): GymApp's React Native binary is shared by every gym. Runtime branding fetch + GymConfigContext means adding a tenant is one database row, not a new App Store submission.
- [Socket.io + Redis pub/sub across PM2 cluster workers — live occupancy without polling](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/socketio-redis-pubsub-pm2-cluster): vanilla Socket.io scales to one process. The Redis adapter (`@socket.io/redis-adapter`) is the patch that makes it work across workers. GymApp's turnstile-tap → dashboard latency: ~50ms.
- [node-hid as a hardware-abstraction layer — decoupling NFC scanners from the API](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/node-hid-nfc-scanner-bridge-pattern): a tiny Node service on a Raspberry Pi reads card UIDs via `node-hid` and POSTs `/api/visits`. The Pi knows hardware; the API knows business logic. Neither knows the other's details.
- [Brand-as-filesystem-config — adding a tenant without a code change](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/social-command-center-brand-as-filesystem-config): Social Command Center adds a brand by dropping a JSON config + knowledge-base directory. BullMQ orchestrator walks each brand through a six-stage pipeline. No admin UI for tenants; a filesystem is faster.
- [Audit middleware that never blocks the real write — best-effort logging done right](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/audit-middleware-never-blocks-real-write): Pilates Studio's audit middleware runs after the main operation, catches failures locally, never rolls back the real write. Losing a booking to a slow audit table is not an acceptable failure mode.
- [Booking-flow status transitions — auto-promoting from the waitlist on cancellation](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/booking-flow-status-transitions-waitlist): Pilates Studio's booking state machine — cancellation atomically promotes the oldest waitlist entry within the same Postgres transaction. Cron sweep handles missed cases. Operator never manually reshuffles attendance.
- [Discipline as the product — architectural rules that survive every refactor](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/discipline-as-the-product): CleanSlate's rules enforced structurally — route files dispatch to services, services own all data ops, components never touch Supabase, money is always cents, phones always E.164. TypeScript types + ESLint imports + RLS policies, not conventions.
- [Four Vercel cron endpoints — the minimum for a SaaS that runs itself](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/four-vercel-crons-saas-runs-itself): CleanSlate's operator never logs in for admin work. Four crons handle trial reminders, overdue invoices, recurring job generation, pre-job SMS. Each idempotent. Operator's time goes to selling and supporting.
- [MMKV vs AsyncStorage on the cold-start hot path — when synchronous storage wins](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/mmkv-vs-asyncstorage-cold-start-hot-path): AsyncStorage is async — every read crosses the RN bridge, adding latency to cold-start critical-path code. MMKV is synchronous, encrypted, ~30x faster. Dabei uses it for auth, drafts, and last-known map region.
- [Vibe Checks as a first-class entity — when a social mechanic is the product](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/vibe-checks-first-class-entity): Dabei's vibe checks are attendance-verified, time-bounded (48 hours), unique-per-rater ratings. `submit_vibe_check` Postgres RPC enforces all of it atomically. Reputation flows from shared experiences, not follower counts.
- [Splitting the data layer into reads, writes, and actions — the three-services pattern](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/three-services-data-layer-hangout-crud-queries-actions): Dabei splits each entity's data layer into three services — hangout-crud (writes), hangout-queries (reads), hangout-actions (cross-entity transactions). RLS reasoning becomes local; tests target boundaries; no 1500-line god-services.
- [A Three.js Hyperspeed hero for a one-day brand build — when scope and ambition meet](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/threejs-hyperspeed-hero-one-day-build): Kërçishta Garage commits to one signature visual + restraint everywhere else. ~150 lines of React + Three.js; bundle weight is the real cost; the hero gives a one-day build presence.
- [Hidden admin CRMs gated by a passphrase plus Bearer token — when minimal auth is right-sized](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/hidden-admin-crm-passphrase-bearer-token): for single-operator small business CRMs, passphrase + Bearer token in sessionStorage is appropriate security. Anything heavier is overhead without proportional safety. Match auth complexity to threat model.
- [Quiz state in URL params — backend-touch deferred until final submit](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/url-params-as-form-state): Klodi Trainer's multi-step fitness quiz puts every answer in URL query parameters. Refresh preserves state; sharing a URL shares state; backend doesn't get touched until final submit. No state-management library, no backend draft system.
- [Route → service → data — the layer discipline that scales solo development](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/service-layer-discipline-route-service-data): the three-layer architecture discipline that survives across React, Express, React Native, and Business Central work. ESLint no-restricted-imports turns convention into compile-time enforcement.
- [How many tests is enough — the 594-test budget on a solo project](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/test-budget-594-tests-pilates-discipline): test count isn't a target. Cover the unhappy paths your users will hit. Pilates Studio ends at 594 across Vitest unit + supertest API integration + Playwright E2E + component tests. Skip the obvious-correct; cover what breaks.
- [Playwright "walker" tests — screenshotting every route on every device](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/playwright-walker-tests-screenshot-every-route): walker tests visit every route across desktop + iPhone 12 + Pixel 5 viewports and capture screenshots. Catches responsive-layout regressions, broken links, and missing translation strings that per-feature E2E tests miss.
- [Postgres RLS vs middleware auth gates — when each one wins](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/postgres-rls-vs-middleware-auth-comparison): comparison table for per-row scope, cross-cutting concerns, race conditions, testability. Use both as defense in depth — RLS at the database, middleware at the API, UI checks for UX only.
- [better-sqlite3 vs Turso (libsql) — when each one wins in production](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/better-sqlite3-vs-turso-libsql-production): in-process SQLite vs networked edge-replicated libsql. Pilates Studio uses better-sqlite3 in dev + Turso in prod via Prisma adapter swap.
- [Claude vs OpenAI vs Gemini for code-fix agents — which model does what best](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/claude-vs-openai-vs-gemini-for-code-agents): Anthropic Claude wins on code reasoning + uncertainty calibration; OpenAI on structured extraction; Gemini on long-context and cost. Per-stage routing beats picking one model for everything.
- [BullMQ vs Trigger.dev vs Inngest — comparing job queues for production](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/bullmq-vs-trigger-dev-vs-inngest-job-queues): BullMQ for self-hosted high-volume Redis-backed queueing. Trigger.dev for managed code-defined durable workflows. Inngest for event-driven systems with strong tracing. When you don't need any of these.
- [Supabase RLS vs Firestore Rules — comparing database-layer authorization](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/supabase-rls-vs-firestore-rules-comparison): SQL policy expressions vs JavaScript-like DSL. Supabase wins on relational data + complex joins; Firestore wins on offline-first mobile + native real-time subscriptions. Pick by data model fit, not rules language preference.
- [Express as a Vercel catch-all — one codebase, two runtime models](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/express-vercel-catch-all-one-codebase-two-runtimes): Pilates Studio's API ships as a Vercel serverless catch-all at `api/[[...path]].ts`. Same Express app, long-lived locally + serverless function in prod. Adapter pattern swaps the database connection model.
- [Single App.tsx — when scope discipline beats abstraction](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/single-app-tsx-when-scope-discipline-beats-abstraction): Kërçishta Garage's whole app fits in one App.tsx. The discipline is matching structure to scope, not maximizing abstraction. Right pattern for one-day brand sites; wrong for multi-month products.
- [GDPR-compliant soft delete with retention crons — the audit-friendly cleanup pattern](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/gdpr-soft-delete-retention-crons): advance.al soft-deletes users (sets deleted_at + middleware filters them out); daily Vercel cron hard-deletes after 30 days. GDPR right-to-erasure satisfied; operational benefits of recoverable deletes preserved.
- [What 10 production projects taught me about solo shipping](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/solo-shipping-architecture-trade-offs-10-projects): retrospective. What paid back from day one (layer discipline, boundary types, DB-level auth, test budget on unhappy paths). What I'd defer (multi-environment infra, custom admin UIs, microservices, component libraries). What changed my mind.
- [How freelance software developer rates work in Germany — Stundensatz reality check](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/freelance-developer-rate-card-germany): honest 2026 picture — €90-€150/hour for senior full-stack, +€20-€40 for AI specialization, €120-€180 for tier-3 Business Central. Werkvertrag (fixed-deliverable) pricing has a 10-50% risk premium depending on scope clarity.
- [What a freelance engineer's portfolio should actually show — beyond the screenshot grid](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/freelance-engineer-portfolio-what-to-show): live URLs, public repos, test counts with CI status, architectural decision paragraphs, solo vs team contribution. Screenshots are decoration; specifics are evidence.
- [What good AI engineering looks like — beyond the demo](https://jurgenhalili.dev/notes/what-good-ai-engineering-looks-like): production AI is everything around the model call — eval frameworks, cost telemetry, multi-provider routing, structured output enforcement, failure-mode handling, observability. The model is the smallest line of code; the engineering is everything around it.
